# Santatara Sutta (Iti 73 (It 3.24 PTS It 61))

**ID:** Iti 73 (It 3.24 PTS It 61)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Santatara Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Santatara Sutta* (*Santatarasutta*, Iti 73) is a short discourse located in the *Itivuttaka* (It 3.24, PTS It 61). The sutta sets forth a hierarchical contemplation of peace: formless phenomena (*arūpā*) are described as more peaceful than material forms (*rūpehi*), while cessation (*nirodha*) is more peaceful than formless phenomena [Windisch 1889]. As is typical of the collection, the prose teaching is summarized in verse, warning of beings who are bound to form or established in the formless without comprehending cessation (*nirodham appajānantā*) [Windisch 1889]. In his 1889 editio princeps for the Pali Text Society, Ernst Windisch noted manuscript confusions and shared interpolations involving the text of sutta 73 across certain witnesses [Windisch 1889].

 The formula declaring formless attainments to be more peaceful (*āruppā santatarā*) is directly attested in the text of Snp 3.12 [Anderson and Smith 1913]. In automated text-reuse analysis, DharmaNexus detects extensive Pali-internal reuse with the *Dhātu Sutta* (*Itivuttaka* 51), which shares nearly identical prose and verse segments (§4.1–6.1 ↔ §3.1–5.1 with 0.98 similarity), alongside introductory stock phrasing shared with the *Bhidura Sutta* (Iti 77) and the *Avuṭṭhika Sutta* (Iti 75) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records machine-generated cross-language alignments with the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (*Zhong ahan jing*, T 26) [DharmaNexus].
